phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-27, recorded on this key because the extractor does not emit destructors: the MOVE CONSTRUCTOR and move-assignment carry the same defect and do surface here.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: an `rclcpp` subscription is owned by a `shared_ptr` the node holds, so destroying or relocating the user's handle cannot leave the executor dispatching into it.

OURS: the destructor (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/subscription.hpp:451`) unregisters only in POLL mode — `if (initialized_ && !callback_mode_)`. In callback mode it clears a flag and nothing else, and NO unregister FFI exists at all (`grep -n "unregister\|deregister" packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/detail/nros_cpp_ffi.h` finds nothing). The arena still holds `&out` as its dispatch context. The move constructor (`:465`) and move-assignment (`:480`) are the same shape: they copy the callback fields, SKIP the relocate for callback mode, and clear `other.initialized_` — leaving the arena pointing at the moved-from object.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: RUNTIME UB, unattributable. The next `spin_once` calls the trampoline with a pointer to a destroyed or moved-from object, at an arbitrary later tick, with nothing naming the subscription. THE ONLY GUARD IS PROSE — the class comment at `:461` and a `@param`-level "CONSTRAINT: do not move `out` after this returns" at `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/node.hpp:581`. No `= delete`, no `static_assert`, no runtime check. RFC-0089 says a refusal fires at the earliest point the defect is KNOWABLE, and for a move that point is the TYPE: deleting the move operations in callback mode makes it a compile error. (The `rclcpp::Node` adapter path is safe by construction — `owned_entities_` pins the cell for the node's lifetime.) Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

DISPOSITION REFUSE-LOUD, recorded in the field. For a move the defect is knowable from the TYPE, which RFC-0089 makes the earliest point loudness is available: `= delete` the move constructor and move-assignment in callback mode, so relocating a dispatching subscription is a compile error naming the constraint, instead of a comment asking the user not to.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) — refuse-loud -> adopt-bounded, because a refusal that is only OWED is not a refusal. The paragraph above records the decision (delete the move operations in callback mode); nothing in the header does it yet, and a row reads as the shipped state.

WHAT THE COMPILER POINTS AT: the constructor set. Ours is the default constructor (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/subscription.hpp:505`), a move constructor and move-assignment (`:465`, `:480`), and deleted copies (`:549`). Upstream's `Subscription(node_base, type_support, topic, qos, callback, options, ...)` is not among them, so naming it is `no matching constructor` — and a ported file rarely does: rclcpp constructs subscriptions through `Node::create_subscription`, which is `cpp:Node::create_subscription`'s row.

THE ENVELOPE, and the half that is NOT loud: a callback-mode subscription must not be moved after registration (the arena holds `this` as the trampoline context) and the only guard is prose (`:461`, and `node.hpp`'s CONSTRAINT note). RFC-0089 puts that refusal at the TYPE; until the `= delete` lands this row is adopt-bounded with the envelope stated here and in the header, and the deletion stays owed.

AMENDED 2026-09-18 (phase-456 W2b), and the line numbers above are pre-split. HALF THE ROW IS NOW MOOT AND HALF IS SHARPER. Moot: the destructor's `if (initialized_ && !callback_mode_)` is gone — this class no longer holds a poll subscriber, so the destructor releases nothing and the move operations relocate nothing. Sharper: the remaining hazard is exactly the one this row names, with no second case to hide behind. The out-ref creators still hand the arena `&out`, so moving a registered object still leaves it dispatching into the source address, and the guard is still prose. The `= delete` this row records as OWED is now writable without a `callback_mode_` test, because every object of this type is a registration; it is still not written, so the disposition stays `adopt-bounded`. The returning `rclcpp::Node::create_subscription` has no such hazard at all (phase-456 W1 put the capture in the arena and it hands back a value).
